FILING_DESTINATION.finding: This route has two destinations in a fixed legal sequence and the packet states one of them. Stage one is fully named on the packet's own face: the BCI instruction page prints "UTAH BUREAU OF CRIMINAL IDENTIFICATION, 4315 South 2700 West, Suite 1300, Taylorsville, Utah 84129" and bciexpungements@utah.gov. Stage two — the district or justice court that decided the case — is named nowhere: the 1,167-byte participant-instructions.md has no "Where you file this" section at all, and the only trace is the prefilled caption, which under this factory's settled standard is evidence but is not the instructions naming a destination. Amendment A1's test is answered first and it is answered yes: the committed track registry holds "Two destinations in a fixed legal sequence ... the participant first applies to BCI, which decides eligibility and issues a certificate valid for 180 days. The participant then files the expungement petition ... in the district or justice court that decided the case." The repository establishes it, so the packet must state it. The sibling ut_pet_no_charges-set, which ships nearly the same forms, states both stages and the 180-day window in full, so this is a gap in this packet rather than a limit of what is knowable.

SERVICE.finding: The packet states neither who must receive a copy nor how, and names no authority to ask. The 1,167-byte participant-instructions.md mentions service only twice, both times as a timing caveat — "Service method, address, date, and certification only after service occurs" and "service certifications ... remain protected" — which tells the participant when to fill a certificate in, not whom to serve. The packet does carry form 1146XX, Acceptance of Service – Expungement (Prosecutor), but a form's presence is not a direction: nothing on the delivered pages says the participant must send the prosecutor a copy, or by what method. The repository establishes the rule — the committed track registry states "The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve" — and the sibling ut_pet_no_charges-set packet states the recipient and the method in terms and names the Utah State Courts Self-Help Center (888-583-0009) besides. Under the determination, silence fails and a rule the repository holds must be stated.

whatTheInstructionsSayAboutService: Service method, address, date, and certification only after service occurs
evidence.trackRegistryService: The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Met, but only just. The instructions state where the platform stops in both required senses: they name the facts it will not supply (a ten-item list, each "supply them from your own records or complete them when the named event occurs; do not guess") and the field classes it will not sign (signatures, signature dates, service certifications, court-only, agency-only, prosecutor-only, victim fields and optional third-party authorizations). What is missing, and is recorded here rather than waved through, is the participant-facing statement that the artifact carries no approval — the sibling ut_pet_no_charges-set and ut_pet_traffic-set both carry a "What this packet is not" paragraph saying the packet is not legal advice, is not filed for the participant and decides nothing, and this one does not. The control plane does say it: approval-request.json records status REQUESTED, generationAllowed false, runtimeSelectable false, independentVisualReviewRequired true, outputLegalApprovalRequired true, zero commercial routes opened.

rows.whyNotAPass: Thirteen of fifteen obligations pass, measured here from the bytes and from the mounted corpus. Two fail on the same cause: this family ships a 1,167-byte participant-instructions.md that is a required-before-filing list and nothing else, while the two Utah families with full instructions ship the same forms and answer both questions. The repair is to give this family the filing-destination and service sections its siblings already carry, keyed to this route's own two-stage sequence — one shared fix across ut_pet_acquittal-set, ut_pet_conviction-set and ut_pet_dismissed_with_prejudice-set, and ut_pet_limitations-set shares the same stub and the same artifact bytes.
